title: ruling 5560224701 assigned a contract-review input row naming the snapshot diff as a Clause-② signal, and nothing carries it
body:
## What the ruling assigned, and what appears to have no carrier

Ruling `5560224701` (director batch #60, 2026-09-06, maintainer verbatim 「同意」) chose a readable declaration-text snapshot for every `@objectstack/spec` export, and it named the mechanism that makes such a snapshot mean anything, verbatim:

> A snapshot diff is not something a PR "accepts": it makes the PR a Clause-② carrier (`needs:contract-review`), and the contract-review seat reads the diff and rules minor/major. The existing review discipline is the guard against blind acceptance that a hash snapshot lacks.

and assigned the follow-up, also verbatim:

> The contract-review reference (`references/contract-review.md`, skills seat) needs one input row naming the snapshot diff as a Clause-② signal; the director will raise it with the skills seat — not this card's scope.

The snapshot itself has now landed work behind it: PR #18971 (card #16045) creates `packages/spec/api-surface-declarations/**` (17 shards, 5,336 declaration blocks) and retires `api-surface-signatures.json`. That PR correctly did NOT wire the new artefact into any Clause-② detector, because the ruling put that row out of its scope by name.

## Measured consequence: the guard is currently inert

Measured by the at-tier contract reviewer on PR #18971's head `b33898f5d8d0dc8eff732eb8ac26452506b8622e` (2026-09-18T0902Z), and recorded here because it is the ruling's own load-bearing mechanism:

- `PUBLISHED_SURFACES` in `scripts/pm/check-widening-tells.mjs` is `REGEN_ARTIFACTS.filter(row => row.check === 'check:api-surface')` — a literal filter on the check name.
- The new artefact's `REGEN_ARTIFACTS` row carries `check: 'check:api-surface-declarations'`, so it is off that surface **by construction**, not by omission.

⇒ Until the assigned row exists, a pull request that regenerates the shards beside a reshaped declaration and declares `Clause-②: no` raises no tell and passes `check-clause2-carriers`. The snapshot is readable, but nothing turns reading it into an obligation — which is precisely the "blind acceptance" the ruling chose text over a hash to prevent.

## Why this is filed rather than asked in a comment

A cross-seat request is work, and work belongs on a card in the target lane's queue rather than in a comment that no sweep reads. The ruling says "the director will raise it"; this card exists so that the assignment has a carrier regardless of whether that hand-off happened.

⛔ This card does not prescribe the mechanism. Whether the signal should be the reference-doc input row alone (as the ruling says), or additionally something mechanised such as a `PUBLISHED_SURFACES` entry or a dedicated tell, is the skills seat's call — the `domain:spec` seat has no standing to design it, and the ruling did not delegate that choice here.

## Dedup note

⚠️ **I did not dedupe this, and my one instrument was weak — do not read it as an absence.** I listed 49 open `domain:skills` cards and matched TITLES only against `snapshot|contract-review|clause|api-surface`; 6 titles matched and none was this assignment (they concern `check-clause2-carriers` defects, `check-single-claim-paths`, `os-dev.md`, and a separate charter conflict). Bodies were not read, closed cards were not read, and `/search/*` is 403 in this session (sessions are bound to their configured repositories), so a card with a differently-worded title would not have shown up. If this duplicates an existing card, close it as the duplicate and keep the older one.

Dedup words: `contract-review.md`, `snapshot diff`, `Clause-② signal`, `PUBLISHED_SURFACES`, `api-surface-declarations`

Provenance: filed by the `domain:spec` seat 3 (session_019srGWGCBBCBHqcDoRZpQRh) out of the at-tier contract review of PR #18971, 2026-09-18T0913Z. ⛔ No `domain:*` or priority set here — this seat is an execution seat and does not route or grade bare cards; the ruling quoted above names the owning seat, so the routing is the ruling's, not a judgement of mine.
